case.pattern_description: Coordinated multi-card exploitation by a single specific device (Samsung SM-G935F) operating behind an anonymous proxy, cycling across multiple compromised debit cards to conduct unauthorized online purchases. This matches the identical undocumented fraud typology confirmed in prior closed cases CC-2649, CC-2971, CC-2985, and CC-3035. The pattern does not follow standard card testing or account takeover sequences but represents syndicated cross-card abuse.

evidence.claim: Device D004630 connects card C01289-K1 to 6 other cards active between 2016-11-14 and 2016-11-17 (C01996-K2, C10326-K1, C02975-K1, C13487-K1, C09975-K1, C08168-K1), all appearing as New device and operating behind anonymous proxy IP_PROXY:ANONYMOUS, and belongs to device ring 57672119.

Device D004630 has 4 prior closed cases (CC-2649, CC-2971, CC-2985, CC-3035), all confirmed fraud under pattern undocumented involving unauthorized online purchases from Samsung SM-G935F on Chrome for Android behind an anonymous proxy.

Flagged transaction 3467346 was conducted on device D004630 (SM-G935F Build/NRD90M | Android 7.0 | chrome 62.0 for android | 1920x1080), which was marked as New for the account and used an anonymous proxy (IP_PROXY:ANONYMOUS).

The holder baseline for C01289-K1|472|139 has 0 prior transactions, representing the first transaction under this anchor day, and departs from the card history where 24 of 25 transactions were in-person retail product W.
Transaction 3467346 received a low model score of 0.027 with historical fraud rate of 0.006 and legacy risk score of 0.15, reflecting that the fraud model cannot detect cross-card graph linkages.
Transaction 3467346 occurred in billing region 472, which matches all 25 prior transactions on card C01289-K1.
The flagged amount of $89.53 is comparable to legitimate in-person transactions on card C01289-K1 ($49.05 on 2016-11-14 and $107.93 on 2016-11-18).

evidence.claim: Rule R9: Undocumented patterns: Rule R9: Undocumented patterns. When activity fits none of the known patterns but the evidence shows coordinated or repeated abuse across customers, recommend `CREATE_CASE`, `FILE_REPORT`, and `ESCALATE_TO_ANALYST`, and describe the pattern in your own words. Do not force it into a known category.

Rule R6: Shared origin: Rule R6: Shared origin. When several cards show fraud from the same device profile, the same billing region, or the same recipient email in one window, name the shared element, recommend `CREATE_CASE` and `FILE_REPORT`, and `MONITOR_CONNECTED_CARDS` for every card that shares it.

case.summary: Transaction 3467346 ($89.53) on card C01289-K1 was flagged via monitoring due to the use of device D004630 from device ring 57672119, appearing as a new device behind an anonymous proxy. Graph analysis revealed that device D004630 connects to six other active cards and four confirmed-fraud closed cases (CC-2649, CC-2971, CC-2985, and CC-3035). However, the transaction received a low model score of 0.027, matched the cardholder's usual billing region 472, and aligned with typical spending amounts. With a calculated fraud probability of 0.163, the verdict remains uncertain, leading to case creation, monitoring of connected cards, and escalation to an analyst.
